taxon_hygiene.title: Colin Kennedy
taxon_hygiene.description: Colin Kennedy is Chief Executive of The Mary Peters Trust, a leading Northern Ireland Sporting Charity. He started his career with the Halifax Building Society and rose to the level of Group Manager Northern Ireland before becoming Chief Financial Officer of one of Irelands largest Healthcare Companies. After selling this Company, he worked as a Consultant with various Organisations and Companies within the Private, Public and Voluntary Sectors including: Northern Ireland Voluntary Trust, The Community Foundation for Northern Ireland, The Millennium Awards Scheme, Belfast Women’s Training Services, The Ulster Sport and Recreation Trust and the General Dental Council. He is currently a member of the Nursing and Midwifery Council Fitness to Practice Panel, a member of the Mental Health Review Tribunal for Northern Ireland, a Commissioner on the Parades Commission for Northern Ireland and a member of the King George VI Youth Council in Northern Ireland. Colin has an MSc (Executive Leadership) from University of Ulster and is married with one son, living in County Down, Northern Ireland. items.legislation_title: Tobacco and Vapes Act 2026

commencements.subject: Tobacco vending machines
commencements.description: Creates an offence for those managing or controlling premises with a tobacco vending machine.

commencements.subject: Sale of unpackaged cigarettes
commencements.description: Prohibates tobacco retailers from selling cigarettes not in original packaging.

commencements.subject: Ban on manufacture of snus etc
commencements.description: Bans the manufacture of snus and similar oral tobacco products in England and Wales.

commencements.subject: Ban on sales of snus etc
commencements.description: Bans selling, offering, or exposing for sale relevant oral tobacco products in England and Wales.

commencements.subject: Possession of snus etc with intent to supply
commencements.description: Makes it an offence to possess relevant oral tobacco products with intent to supply them in business.

commencements.qualification: in force in so far as not already in force
commencements.subject: Sale of vaping or nicotine products to under 18s
commencements.description: Makes it an offence in England and Wales, with an age-verification defence, to sell vaping or nicotine products to under-18s.

commencements.subject: Purchase of vaping or nicotine products on behalf of under 18s
commencements.description: Makes it an offence in England and Wales for adults to buy vaping or nicotine products for under-18s.

commencements.subject: Vaping and nicotine product vending machines
commencements.description: Creates offence for managing premises with vape or nicotine vending machines; exempts vape in mental health hospitals.

commencements.qualification: in force in so far as not already in force
commencements.subject: Displays of products or prices in England
commencements.description: Grants the Secretary of State power to regulate retailers' display of relevant products and empty packaging in England.

commencements.qualification: in force in so far as not already in force
commencements.subject: Displays of products or prices in Wales
commencements.description: Grants Welsh Ministers a power to regulate display of relevant products and packaging in Wales.

commencements.subject: Free distribution and discount of products
commencements.description: Creates an offence for giving away or discounting products or coupons to promote a relevant product.

commencements.subject: Restricted premises orders
commencements.description: Allows prosecutors to seek restricted premises orders against persistent offenders.

commencements.subject: Restricted premises orders: interested persons
commencements.description: Gives interested persons the right to be notified about restricted premises order applications and to make court objections.

commencements.subject: Restricted premises orders: appeals
commencements.description: Grants a right to appeal to the Crown Court against restricted premises orders.

commencements.subject: Breach of restricted premises orders
commencements.description: Creates a criminal offence for selling anything in breach of a restricted premises order, with reasonable steps defence.

commencements.qualification: in force in so far as not already in force
commencements.subject: Power to extend restricted premises orders in Wales
commencements.description: Grants Welsh Ministers power to extend restricted premises orders to new tobacco and vaping offences in Wales.

commencements.subject: Restricted sale orders
commencements.description: Introduces a restricted sale order to ban persistent offenders from selling tobacco, herbal smoking, and cigarette products.

commencements.subject: Restricted sale orders: appeals
commencements.description: Creates a right to appeal restricted sale orders to the Crown Court.

commencements.subject: Breach of restricted sale orders
commencements.description: Creates an offence for breaching a restricted sale order, with a reasonable-steps defence and a fine.

commencements.subject: Liability of others for certain offences committed by bodies
commencements.description: Makes individuals criminally liable for a body's offence if they consent or connive to it.

taxon_hygiene.description: This list covers a large amount of Chancery work which is separate from the Business List. It includes the following types of work: Property landlord and tenant residential landlord and tenant commercial trespass/squatters mortgages land registry land – including title, easements, restrictive covenants orders for sale to enforce charging orders Trusts of Land and Appointment of Trustees Act 1996 (TOLATA) Trusts variation of trusts removal of trustees claims against trustees for breach of trust issues of construction/rectification trustees/personal representatives seeking directions including Beddoe applications (a type of application made by trustees) disputes about trust property applications for prospective costs order (deciding costs issues in advance) charities applications for administration order (appointing a person to manage a company that is in financial difficulty) Probate inheritance disputes (known as contentious probate claims) rectification of wills (cases against the way a solicitor has prepared a will) substitution or removal of personal representatives cases involving the Inheritance Act cases involving the Presumption of Death Act Cases are started in the Chancery Division. Who we are We are a specialist court within the Business and Property Courts of the High Court of Justice. We are based at the Rolls Building in London. Cases in the Property, Trusts and Probate List are managed by the Chancery Masters and heard by the Chancery Division judges. taxon_hygiene.title: Administrative Court
taxon_hygiene.description: We review decisions made by people or bodies with a public law function, eg local authorities and regulatory bodies. We can: carry out a judicial review of decisions made by other courts, tribunals and public bodies hear challenges to decisions made by certain people or bodies (eg ministers or local government) where legislation has given the right to challenge We also hear: applications for ‘habeas corpus’, (a legal procedure where the court decides to rule on whether the detention of an individual is legal applications to prevent someone who continues to initiate groundless legal proceedings (a ‘vexatious litigant’) from continuing to do so without first obtaining permission from a court all applications under the Coroners Act 1988 (which deals with the appointment and conduct of coroners) appeals ‘by way of case stated’ from the Crown Court or magistrates’ courts (where our opinion is sought on a particular point of law where a mistake may have been made) applications for an order to imprison a person for contempt of court appeals under the Extradition Act 2003 (which deals with extradition requests to and from the United Kingdom and bail) appeals against decisions made by some professional bodies, eg the Nursing and Midwifery Council applications for ‘restraint orders’ or ‘certificates of inadequacy’ where assets have been frozen or confiscated We also contain a specialist Planning Court which handles judicial reviews of decisions about planning permission and other challenges to planning decisions. Who we are We are a specialist court within the King’s Bench Division of the High Court of Justice. We are based at the Royal Courts of Justice, London and also at centres in Birmingham, Cardiff, Leeds and Manchester. Cases may be heard by one High Court judge or by a ‘Divisional Court’ which consists of 2 or more judges, normally a High Court Judge and a Lord Justice of Appeal. taxon_hygiene.title: Dr Ali Hashtroudi
taxon_hygiene.description: Dr Ali Hashtroudi, FFOM MSc LLM is a consultant occupational physician and Fellow of the Faculty of Occupational Medicine. He is the Clinical Director of Occupational Health and Safety Services, Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust. He is the Medical Officer for South Yorkshire Fire and Rescue Service. He is an Honorary Senior Lecturer at Kings College London ( KCL ). He is the Head of the National School of Occupational Health at Health Education England. He is an Appointed Doctor under several legislations for Health and Safety Executive. He is a Health Examiner and Medical Supervisor for the GMC . His other appointments include membership of the Faculty of Occupational Medicine Ethics Committee, Chair of the Higher Education Occupational Practitioners and Occupational Health Expert at the UK Advisory Panel for Healthcare Workers Infected with Bloodborne Viruses. He lectures for the Masters course in Organisational Psychiatry and Psychology at the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology and Neurosciences, KCL . His academic work includes publications in peer reviewed journals in the subject of occupational medicine and has presented nationally and internationally. He has authored a chapter in Fitness for Work a leading textbook in occupational medicine. He has a broad range of educational activities including clinical and education supervision of undergraduate students and specialty registrars in occupational medicine. He was previously the Faculty of Occupational Medicine Regional Specialty Advisor for South Thames region. In his current role as the Head of National School of Occupational Health he is responsible for the quality assurance of the training of the future occupational health practitioners. He served as a member of the Board of the Faculty of Occupational Medicine between 2007 and 2009, and on the NHS Health at Work Network Board since its inception in 2011 until 2017. He has a keen interest in the health of healthcare workers, emergency workers and students. He has a wide range of research interests including mental health and work, and biological hazards. He has supervised academic work of students from undergraduate level to PhD. He is a member of the Editorial Board of Egyptian Journal of Occupational Medicine.

findings.title: Administrative Court
findings.description: We review decisions made by people or bodies with a public law function, eg local authorities and regulatory bodies. We can: carry out a judicial review of decisions made by other courts, tribunals and public bodies hear challenges to decisions made by certain people or bodies (eg ministers or local government) where legislation has given the right to challenge We also hear: applications for ‘habeas corpus’, (a legal procedure where the court decides to rule on whether the detention of an individual is legal applications to prevent someone who continues to initiate groundless legal proceedings (a ‘vexatious litigant’) from continuing to do so without first obtaining permission from a court all applications under the Coroners Act 1988 (which deals with the appointment and conduct of coroners) appeals ‘by way of case stated’ from the Crown Court or magistrates’ courts (where our opinion is sought on a particular point of law where a mistake may have been made) applications for an order to imprison a person for contempt of court appeals under the Extradition Act 2003 (which deals with extradition requests to and from the United Kingdom and bail) appeals against decisions made by some professional bodies, eg the Nursing and Midwifery Council applications for ‘restraint orders’ or ‘certificates of inadequacy’ where assets have been frozen or confiscated We also contain a specialist Planning Court which handles judicial reviews of decisions about planning permission and other challenges to planning decisions. Who we are We are a specialist court within the King’s Bench Division of the High Court of Justice. We are based at the Royal Courts of Justice, London and also at centres in Birmingham, Cardiff, Leeds and Manchester. Cases may be heard by one High Court judge or by a ‘Divisional Court’ which consists of 2 or more judges, normally a High Court Judge and a Lord Justice of Appeal. findings.title: Dr Ali Hashtroudi
findings.description: Dr Ali Hashtroudi, FFOM MSc LLM is a consultant occupational physician and Fellow of the Faculty of Occupational Medicine. He is the Clinical Director of Occupational Health and Safety Services, Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust. He is the Medical Officer for South Yorkshire Fire and Rescue Service. He is an Honorary Senior Lecturer at Kings College London ( KCL ). He is the Head of the National School of Occupational Health at Health Education England. He is an Appointed Doctor under several legislations for Health and Safety Executive. He is a Health Examiner and Medical Supervisor for the GMC . His other appointments include membership of the Faculty of Occupational Medicine Ethics Committee, Chair of the Higher Education Occupational Practitioners and Occupational Health Expert at the UK Advisory Panel for Healthcare Workers Infected with Bloodborne Viruses. He lectures for the Masters course in Organisational Psychiatry and Psychology at the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology and Neurosciences, KCL . His academic work includes publications in peer reviewed journals in the subject of occupational medicine and has presented nationally and internationally. He has authored a chapter in Fitness for Work a leading textbook in occupational medicine. He has a broad range of educational activities including clinical and education supervision of undergraduate students and specialty registrars in occupational medicine. He was previously the Faculty of Occupational Medicine Regional Specialty Advisor for South Thames region. In his current role as the Head of National School of Occupational Health he is responsible for the quality assurance of the training of the future occupational health practitioners. He served as a member of the Board of the Faculty of Occupational Medicine between 2007 and 2009, and on the NHS Health at Work Network Board since its inception in 2011 until 2017. He has a keen interest in the health of healthcare workers, emergency workers and students. He has a wide range of research interests including mental health and work, and biological hazards. He has supervised academic work of students from undergraduate level to PhD. He is a member of the Editorial Board of Egyptian Journal of Occupational Medicine.

findings.title: Colin Kennedy
findings.description: Colin Kennedy is Chief Executive of The Mary Peters Trust, a leading Northern Ireland Sporting Charity. He started his career with the Halifax Building Society and rose to the level of Group Manager Northern Ireland before becoming Chief Financial Officer of one of Irelands largest Healthcare Companies. After selling this Company, he worked as a Consultant with various Organisations and Companies within the Private, Public and Voluntary Sectors including: Northern Ireland Voluntary Trust, The Community Foundation for Northern Ireland, The Millennium Awards Scheme, Belfast Women’s Training Services, The Ulster Sport and Recreation Trust and the General Dental Council. He is currently a member of the Nursing and Midwifery Council Fitness to Practice Panel, a member of the Mental Health Review Tribunal for Northern Ireland, a Commissioner on the Parades Commission for Northern Ireland and a member of the King George VI Youth Council in Northern Ireland. Colin has an MSc (Executive Leadership) from University of Ulster and is married with one son, living in County Down, Northern Ireland.
